set.st: Tradition, first printed in 1950: the government's long-delayed land payment arrived as gold coins filling a copper kettle, meant to be shared by the tribe. The dying chief slipped out at night and hid it, then died suddenly without telling where. Many have searched; no find reported. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: The 1950 account does not name the lake. The chief's grave and DAR monument stand by the old Indian school lot near Elbridge: look-only. State land nearby.
